title: Asteroid Apophis: Newton's law of gravity from a video
description: Four years of 99942 Apophis, rendered from NASA/JPL Horizons positions. Watching only the dot, PhysicsLens found Newton's inverse-square law with the Sun's GM within 0.023% of JPL's value. The winning law, written by the agent, also carries a tiny constant push against the motion (8.7e-8 m/s^2). There is nothing to push in space: tested on simulated tracks, a slowing term of this kind comes out when the planets pull on Apophis and at zero (Kepler alone wins) when they don't, so it stands in for the planets' pull, which no candidate law included. Extrapolated 3.3 years, the law puts the 2029 Earth flyby 13 hours after JPL's time; the distance (38,000 km) is far below what one pixel (340,000 km) can resolve. Units: AU and days.
credit: Rendered by PhysicsLens from NASA/JPL Horizons data (JPL Solar System Dynamics); close-approach reference from the JPL CNEOS API
